q: The Constituent Assembly of India met for the first time on which date?
x: The Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946, with Sachchidananda Sinha as temporary chairman. Rajendra Prasad was elected its permanent president on 11 December 1946.
e: First sitting 9 Dec 1946, Constitution adopted 26 Nov 1949, in force 26 Jan 1950.

q: Who was the chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
x: B. R. Ambedkar chaired the seven-member Drafting Committee set up on 29 August 1947. Rajendra Prasad was president of the Constituent Assembly itself.
e: Ambedkar chaired the drafting; Rajendra Prasad chaired the Assembly.

q: The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble by which amendment?
x: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 inserted 'Socialist' and 'Secular' into the description of the Republic and added 'and integrity' after 'unity'.
e: The 42nd is called the 'Mini-Constitution' — it also added the Fundamental Duties.

q: The idea of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from which country?
x: The Directive Principles in Part IV were taken from the Irish Constitution, which had in turn drawn on the Spanish one.
e: Ireland: DPSP. USA: Fundamental Rights. UK: parliamentary system. Canada: strong centre.

q: How many schedules does the Constitution of India have at present?
x: The Constitution began with eight schedules; it now has twelve. The ninth, tenth, eleventh and twelfth were added by later amendments.
e: 8th = languages, 9th = land reform laws, 10th = anti-defection, 11th = panchayats, 12th = municipalities.

q: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form; enforcing any disability arising out of it is an offence punishable by law.
e: 14 equality, 15 no discrimination, 16 equal opportunity, 17 untouchability, 18 titles.

q: Dr B. R. Ambedkar described which Article as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
x: Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution because the other rights would be empty without it.
e: Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right — the right to a remedy.

q: The Right to Education was made a Fundamental Right by which amendment?
x: The 86th Amendment of 2002 inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged six to fourteen.
e: 86th Amendment: Article 21A, ages 6 to 14, and the duty of parents in Article 51A(k).

q: The Right to Property ceased to be a Fundamental Right after which amendment?
x: The 44th Amendment of 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights. It is now a constitutional legal right under Article 300A.
e: Property moved out of Fundamental Rights in 1978 and became Article 300A.

q: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendation of which committee?
x: The Swaran Singh Committee recommended Fundamental Duties, which the 42nd Amendment of 1976 added as Part IVA, Article 51A.
e: Swaran Singh → 42nd Amendment → Part IVA → Article 51A (now eleven duties).

q: The President of India is elected by an electoral college that includes which of the following?
o: All members of Parliament and all MLAs
Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of state legislative assemblies
Only the members of the Lok Sabha
Members of the Lok Sabha and state legislative councils
x: Under Article 54 the electoral college has the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the states, including Delhi and Puducherry. Nominated members and legislative council members do not vote.
e: Nominated members cannot vote for the President — only elected ones.

q: What is the minimum age to be eligible for election as President of India?
x: Article 58 requires the President to be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified for election to the Lok Sabha.
e: 35 for President and Vice-President, 30 for Rajya Sabha, 25 for Lok Sabha.

q: The Council of Ministers of the Union is collectively responsible to which body?
o: The House of the People (Lok Sabha)
x: Article 75(3) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha alone. If the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, the whole ministry must resign.
e: Only the Lok Sabha can bring the government down — the Rajya Sabha cannot.

q: What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha as fixed by the Constitution?
x: Article 80 fixes the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha at 250 — up to 238 representing the states and union territories, plus 12 nominated by the President.
e: Rajya Sabha ceiling 250 (238 + 12 nominated); Lok Sabha ceiling 550.

q: A Money Bill can be introduced only in which House?
x: Under Article 110 a Money Bill may be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and only on the President's recommendation. The Rajya Sabha can keep it for at most fourteen days and may only suggest changes.
e: Money Bills: Lok Sabha only, Rajya Sabha gets 14 days and no veto.

q: At what age does a judge of the Supreme Court of India retire?
x: A Supreme Court judge holds office until the age of 65 under Article 124. A High Court judge retires at 62 under Article 217.
e: Supreme Court 65, High Court 62.

q: Which writ is issued to free a person who has been unlawfully detained?
x: Habeas Corpus means 'you may have the body'. The court orders the detaining authority to produce the person and justify the detention.
e: Habeas Corpus = produce the body; Mandamus = do your duty; Quo Warranto = by what authority.

q: Which is the oldest High Court in India?
x: The Calcutta High Court was established in 1862 and is the oldest in India. Bombay and Madras were set up in the same year but Calcutta was constituted first.
e: Calcutta, Bombay and Madras all date from 1862; Calcutta came first.

q: Panchayati Raj was given constitutional status by which amendment?
x: The 73rd Amendment of 1992 added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule, giving panchayats constitutional status. The 74th did the same for urban local bodies.
e: 73rd = villages (11th Schedule, 29 subjects); 74th = towns (12th Schedule, 18 subjects).

q: Which Article gives the National Capital Territory of Delhi its special constitutional position?
x: Article 239AA, inserted by the 69th Amendment of 1991, created the National Capital Territory of Delhi with a legislative assembly and a council of ministers.
e: 69th Amendment, 1991: Delhi became the NCT under Article 239AA.

q: President's Rule in a state is imposed under which Article?
x: Article 356 allows the President to take over a state's government when its constitutional machinery fails. Article 352 covers national emergency and Article 360 financial emergency.
e: 352 national, 356 state, 360 financial.

q: The Concurrent List in the Seventh Schedule was borrowed from the constitution of which country?
x: The idea of a Concurrent List, on which both the Union and the states may legislate, was taken from the Australian Constitution.
e: Australia gave India the Concurrent List and freedom of trade between states.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed under which Article?
x: Article 148 provides for the Comptroller and Auditor General, appointed by the President and holding office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
e: 148 CAG, 280 Finance Commission, 315 UPSC, 324 Election Commission.

q: The Election Commission of India is established under which Article of the Constitution?
x: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, state legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President in the Election Commission.
e: Article 324 — one Commission for Parliament, states, President and Vice-President.

q: The anti-defection law is contained in which Schedule of the Constitution?
x: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment of 1985, sets out the grounds on which a member of a legislature is disqualified for defection.
e: 52nd Amendment 1985 → Tenth Schedule → anti-defection.

q: Which planet is known as the Morning Star as well as the Evening Star?
x: Venus is the brightest planet in our sky and is seen just before sunrise or just after sunset, which gives it both names. It is also the hottest planet.
e: Venus: brightest, hottest, and spins the 'wrong' way, east to west.

q: Light from the Sun takes approximately how long to reach the Earth?
x: Sunlight covers the roughly 150 million km to Earth in about 8 minutes and 20 seconds. Light from the Moon takes about 1.3 seconds.
e: Sun about 8 minutes, Moon about 1.3 seconds.

q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
x: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
e: Remember west to east: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram.

q: The ozone layer is found in which layer of the atmosphere?
x: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere, roughly 15 to 35 km above the surface, where it absorbs most ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.
e: Weather happens in the troposphere; ozone and jet aircraft belong to the stratosphere.

q: Most of the world's volcanoes and earthquakes occur around which feature?
x: The Pacific Ring of Fire is the belt of plate boundaries around the Pacific Ocean, home to about three-quarters of the world's active volcanoes and most large earthquakes.
e: Ring of Fire = the rim of the Pacific plate, from Chile up to Alaska and down to Indonesia.

q: The standard meridian of India passes through which place?
x: India's standard meridian is 82 degrees 30 minutes East, which passes through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh. Indian Standard Time is five and a half hours ahead of GMT.
e: 82 degrees 30 minutes E through Mirzapur gives IST = GMT + 5:30.

q: Which is the highest mountain peak lying entirely within India?
x: Nanda Devi in Uttarakhand, at 7,816 m, is the highest peak lying wholly inside India. Kanchenjunga is higher but sits on the India-Nepal border, and K2 is in territory India claims but does not administer.
e: Nanda Devi — highest peak completely inside India's own territory.

q: Chilika Lake, the largest brackish water lagoon in India, lies in which state?
x: Chilika Lake on the Odisha coast is India's largest brackish water lagoon and a Ramsar site known for migratory birds and Irrawaddy dolphins.
e: Chilika brackish (Odisha), Wular freshwater (Jammu and Kashmir), Sambhar salt (Rajasthan).

q: Loktak Lake, famous for its floating islands called phumdis, is located in which state?
x: Loktak Lake in Manipur is the largest freshwater lake in north-east India. Its floating mats of vegetation, called phumdis, carry Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park.
e: Loktak, Manipur — phumdis and the floating national park where the sangai deer lives.

q: The southernmost point of India's territory, Indira Point, is located in which island group?
x: Indira Point is at the southern tip of Great Nicobar Island in the Nicobar group. Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of the Indian mainland.
e: Indira Point = southernmost of India; Kanyakumari = southernmost of the mainland.

q: The Khetri region of Rajasthan is known for the mining of which mineral?
x: The Khetri belt in Jhunjhunu district, Rajasthan, is one of India's main copper-producing areas, worked by Hindustan Copper Limited.
e: Khetri copper (Rajasthan), Kolar gold (Karnataka), Jharia coal (Jharkhand).

q: The White Revolution in India is associated with the production of which commodity?
x: The White Revolution, run as Operation Flood from 1970 under Verghese Kurien, made India the world's largest milk producer and built the Amul dairy cooperative model.
e: White milk, Green foodgrains, Blue fish, Yellow oilseeds, Pink prawns.

q: Black soil, also called regur soil, is best suited for the cultivation of which crop?
x: Black or regur soil, formed from the lava of the Deccan Trap, holds moisture well and is the classic cotton soil of Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
e: Regur is also simply called 'black cotton soil'.

q: According to Census 2011, which state has the highest literacy rate in India?
x: Kerala recorded a literacy rate of about 94 per cent in Census 2011, the highest among the states; Bihar was the lowest.
e: Census 2011: Kerala highest literacy, Bihar lowest, national figure about 74 per cent.

q: According to Census 2011, which state has the highest population density in India?
x: Bihar had the highest population density among states in Census 2011, at about 1,106 persons per square kilometre. Delhi has a higher density but is a union territory.
e: Most people: Uttar Pradesh. Most crowded state: Bihar.

q: Which is the longest river in the world?
x: The Nile in Africa, about 6,650 km long, is conventionally taken as the world's longest river. The Amazon carries the greatest volume of water.
e: Nile longest, Amazon largest by volume.

q: India shares its longest international land border with which country?
x: India's border with Bangladesh runs about 4,096 km, the longest it shares with any neighbour. The shortest is with Afghanistan.
e: Longest: Bangladesh. Shortest: Afghanistan.

q: The McMahon Line forms the boundary between India and which country?
x: The McMahon Line, drawn at the Simla Convention of 1914, is the boundary between India and China in the eastern sector, along Arunachal Pradesh.
e: Radcliffe: India-Pakistan. McMahon: India-China. Durand: Pakistan-Afghanistan.
